name: General Compute
description: General Compute is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: General Compute is a privately held AI infrastructure company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $100 million Series A round announced on October 27, 2026, valued the company at $800 million.

General Compute is building a cloud service for running AI models on specialized inference chips, including those made by Cerebras, SambaNova and Positron. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming General Compute
table_note: Valuations are post-money, as reported by TechCrunch at the time of each round.
round_notes: Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures co-led the Series A. In July 2026, General Compute arranged a $400 million debt facility from Upper90, which is not shown in the table.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures co-led the Series A, and FUSE led the seed round. Other investors include Village Global, Carya Venture Partners and BOLD Capital Partners.
spv_sentence: In 2026, four special purpose vehicles formed to invest in General Compute filed with the SEC.
sources: Sources: General Compute's Series A announcement (October 27, 2026); TechCrunch reports dated October 27, 2026 and May 28, 2026; reports by SiliconANGLE (July 2026) and Los Angeles Business Journal (November 2026); and SEC Form D filings.
